claims.content: A JU wants to transfer reporting responsibility for a specific point, line, or area from one JU to another JU.

claims.content: C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report message indicating that the JU with R² specified in the Source TN field has dropped or ceased reporting the track specified in the Reference TN field.
The receiving JU processes the J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report message for the locally held remote track.
Immediately prior to assuming R² for the air or surface track after receipt of the Drop Track message, the receiving JU tests the track for correlation once.
The receiving JU assumes R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
The latest JU to report the point has R² for that point.

claims.content: Diverges from Step 1: if a J3.4 message containing the Track Number is not received for two consecutive periodic updates, another JU may assume reporting responsibility for the contact instead of transfer being initiated by a J7.0 Drop Track message.

Diverges from Step 1: a JU receiving a J2 PPLI message from a JU that has R² may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit if local reporting eligibility remains and no remote report has been received; this includes when the PPLI NPS Indicator is Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure.

Diverges from Step 1: a C² JU with correlated local sensor data assumes R² of an IU when a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, when the NPS Indicator is set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or when Geodetic Position Quality is set to value 0, rather than only upon a J7.0 Drop Track message.

Diverges from Step 1: for a previously reported emergency point, any JU with additional or more current information on the point may report on it through operator action only, providing an alternative to transfer initiation by a J7.0 Drop Track message.

Diverges from Step 4: for an emergency point, if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the unit with R² is declared inactive, or no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may assume R² for the point by operator action only.

Diverges from Step 1: a JU with R² for a non-real-time ballistic missile track relinquishes R² upon receiving a remote real-time track report for that track, instead of using a J7.0 Drop Track message to initiate transfer.

Diverges from Step 1: after applying all other rules, a JU relinquishes R² for a real-time track upon receiving a remote track report with TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose Source TN is greater than the local Source TN, instead of using a J7.0 Drop Track message to initiate transfer.

claims.content: After the C2 JU transmits the J7.0 Drop Track Report message, if the Dropped TN is reported by another IU, own unit retains the Dropped TN as a remote track and does not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds after transmission of the J7.0.

If the correlation test at Step 3 finds a correlation with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the Track Numbers (TNs) are different, the receiving JU transmits a J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message, retains the Source TN from the PPLI message as the Retained TN, and designates the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.

If the correlation test at Step 3 finds a correlation with a track for which another C2 JU has R², the TNs are the same, and the Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, the receiving JU accepts the surveillance track and discards the PPLI message.

If no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from transmission of the correlation request, the correlation is deemed to have failed and all associated processing for the correlation is cancelled.

If a C² JU finds a correlation between received PPLI reports and local sensor data for a track where the C² JU has R², it transmits a J7.2 Correlation message with Response Value (RV) set to 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), retains the Source TN from the PPLI message, drops the surveillance TN, ceases reporting the track, and transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message.
C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local or remote data held indicates an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
For a ballistic missile launch point, if no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another IU may assume R² for the point by operator action only.

Handling of a missing J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message when no further remote-track updates are received is not documented.
Exit or return path after the same-TN Geodetic Position Quality = 0 exception (accept surveillance track and discard PPLI) is not documented.
Recovery or continuation after the 60-second suppression of re-correlation for a remotely reported Dropped TN is not documented.
Exit or return path after an ID conflict prevents automatic correlation is not documented.
Exit or return path after a C² JU with R² transmits J7.2 RV = 1 and a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is not documented.
Exit or return path after correlation timeout cancellation is not documented.
Exit or return path after operator-assisted assumption of R² for a ballistic missile launch point following missed updates is not documented.

claims.content: The JU assuming R² has and retains the reporting responsibility until it is relinquished in accordance with the rules or until the track is dropped.
For a point, the latest JU to report the point has R² for that point.
For a relinquishment to another JU, the originating JU ceases reporting the transferred entity without transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message.
For an emergency point, the JU assuming R² uses the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.

For a ballistic missile track, the JU assuming R² for the track need not assume R² for the associated launch point; the unit no longer holding R² on the ballistic missile track may continue to report the launch point.
